title: Seasonal salinity drift in restored tidal reed beds: a three year sensor record

headings.text: Seasonal salinity drift in restored tidal reed beds: a three year sensor record

key_sentences: We report three years of continuous salinity measurements from eleven sensors placed in two restored reed beds.
Salinity matters because common reed tolerates brackish water only up to a threshold.
We ask whether salinity has changed since restoration, whether any change differs between seaward and landward positions, and whether dry summers leave a lasting mark.
Each sensor was cleaned and checked against a handheld meter every six weeks.
Dry summers were defined as those with less than 70 per cent of the long term mean rainfall between June and August.
Short drops after heavy rain lasted less than ten days in every case.
Two mechanisms could explain the drift.
We thank the site wardens for access and for their help with sensor maintenance.
